narrative:
The model estimated a 71.7% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. That high predicted risk is why your law school application was denied: the decision reflects concern about first-time bar success, not a final judgment of your ability.

The strongest factor was your year-three class standing. You are in the lowest decile, while accepted students averaged around the sixth decile, and this pushed the prediction toward failure. Your year-one class standing was the second most influential factor and also pushed toward failure; you are again in the lowest decile, compared with an accepted-student average near the sixth decile. Your undergraduate GPA of 2.70 was the third most influential factor. Although it is below the accepted-student average of 3.23, it actually pushed the prediction toward passing; however, it was not enough to offset the two class-standing signals. Your gender and race were not used in the prediction.

To improve a future application, focus on strengthening your academic record and demonstrating readiness for bar-level work. Consider additional coursework, academic support, bar-exam preparation, and, if feasible, retaking the LSAT to address the broader profile. Ask admissions for feedback, then reapply after showing concrete improvement.
